text: If, in the friendship of which I speak, one could give to the other, the receiver of the benefit would be the man that obliged his friend; for each of them contending and above all things studying how to be useful to the other, he that administers the occasion is the liberal man, in giving his friend the satisfaction of doing that towards him which above all things he most desires.
author: Michel de Montaigne
translation: Charles Cotton, ed. W. C. Hazlitt, 1877
